LanguageData.LL_GeologicalTerrainTip: On: new maps are reshaped by geological rules. Off: Living Landscapes only reads the terrain that map generation produced. Existing maps are never changed.
LanguageData.LL_GeologicalTerrainDesc: Shapes new maps from geology: lakes sit in basins, rivers run downhill, and valleys and slopes follow drainage. Turn this off if you use a mod that changes map terrain and isn't listed as supported below; plants will still follow the terrain that mod creates. Only affects newly generated maps.
LanguageData.LL_ScatteredRuinsTip: Vanilla's small ruins, shrines and ancient junk scattered across new maps. Off by default while Living Landscapes' terrain is in development; ruins chosen through tile features are unaffected.
LanguageData.LL_PlantEcologyTip: Wild plants follow the ground (wetness, soil depth, slope, sun), grow in clumps around their own kind and shade what grows beneath them. Off: vanilla's wild plant placement. Applies to maps made with Living Landscapes; maps generated without it, and plants of mods that define no habitat, are unaffected.
LanguageData.LL_HabitatStrengthTip: How strongly the ground and shade steer which plants grow where, and how closely they clump. 0% is vanilla, 100% is the full effect. Takes effect on new maps and on regrowth in running games.
LanguageData.LL_SupportedTerrainMods: Supported terrain and world mods active: {0}
LanguageData.LL_UnsupportedTerrainMods: Other mods that change terrain generation: {0}. If maps look wrong, turn geologically driven terrain off.
LanguageData.LL_GameplaySitingTip: Shape what vanilla places around the terrain for play: the start spot on good settlement ground (level, near water, room to farm, defensible), ore in veins that follow the rock and grow rarer with distance, discoveries in interesting ground. Off: vanilla's random placement. Applies to new maps.
